reasons: 1 finding(s) at or above CRITICAL severity

findings.title: HSTS max-age is shorter than 31536000 seconds
findings.description: A short HSTS lifetime leaves visitors unprotected between policy expiry and renewal. Use at least one year (31536000).

remediation.summary: Send Strict-Transport-Security on every HTTPS response with a max-age of at least one year, includeSubDomains and (once you are confident) preload. HSTS closes the SSL-stripping window for returning visitors.
remediation.apache:
<IfModule mod_headers.c>
    Header always set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload"
</IfModule>
remediation.cloudflare: SSL/TLS → Edge Certificates → HSTS: enable, Max-Age 12 months, Include subdomains = On, Preload = On, No-Sniff header = On.

findings.title: HSTS includeSubDomains is missing
findings.description: includeSubDomains prevents attackers from downgrading any sub-domain, including forgotten staging hosts.

remediation.summary: Send Strict-Transport-Security on every HTTPS response with a max-age of at least one year, includeSubDomains and (once you are confident) preload. HSTS closes the SSL-stripping window for returning visitors.
remediation.apache:
<IfModule mod_headers.c>
    Header always set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload"
</IfModule>
remediation.cloudflare: SSL/TLS → Edge Certificates → HSTS: enable, Max-Age 12 months, Include subdomains = On, Preload = On, No-Sniff header = On.

findings.title: Content-Security-Policy is enforced
findings.description: An enforced CSP limits which sources the browser may load resources from.

findings.title: CSP allows 'unsafe-inline' for scripts
findings.description: 'unsafe-inline' re-enables inline <script> execution, which neutralises most of CSP's XSS protection. Replace inline handlers with nonces or hashes.

remediation.summary: Deploy a restrictive Content-Security-Policy built from a nonce or hash based script-src, drop 'unsafe-inline'/'unsafe-eval', and lock down framing with frame-ancestors.  Roll it out with Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only first.
remediation.nginx: add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-$request_id'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'; form-action 'self'; upgrade-insecure-requests" always;
remediation.apache:
<IfModule mod_headers.c>
    Header always set Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'; form-action 'self'"
</IfModule>
remediation.cloudflare: Cloudflare does not synthesise a CSP. Inject it with a Transform Rule (Modify Response Header → Set → Content-Security-Policy) or at your origin.

findings.title: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff is set
findings.description: MIME sniffing is disabled, preventing content-type confusion attacks.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN is set
findings.description: Framing by third-party origins is blocked.

findings.title: Referrer-Policy restricts referrer leakage
findings.description: Cross-origin requests only receive the origin, not the full path.

findings.title: Permissions-Policy header is missing
findings.description: Without Permissions-Policy, embedded third-party frames may request camera, microphone, geolocation and other powerful features.

remediation.summary: Restrict powerful browser features with Permissions-Policy.  Deny everything you do not explicitly need and never grant camera/microphone/geolocation to '*'.
remediation.nginx: add_header Permissions-Policy "accelerometer=(), camera=(), geolocation=(), gyroscope=(), magnetometer=(), microphone=(), payment=(), usb=()" always;
remediation.apache: Header always set Permissions-Policy "accelerometer=(), camera=(), geolocation=(), gyroscope=(), magnetometer=(), microphone=(), payment=(), usb=()"
remediation.cloudflare: Transform Rule → Set response header Permissions-Policy with an explicit allow-list.

findings.title: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin is set
findings.description: The browsing context is isolated from cross-origin openers.

findings.title: Cookies are missing the Secure flag
findings.description: Cookies without Secure are transmitted over plaintext HTTP and can be captured by any on-path attacker. Session cookies must be Secure.

remediation.summary: Every session cookie needs Secure + HttpOnly + SameSite.  Use the __Host- prefix (requires Secure, Path=/ and no Domain attribute) for authentication cookies.
remediation.nginx:
# nginx ≥ 1.19.3 – rewrite flags on all proxied cookies
proxy_cookie_flags ~ secure httponly samesite=strict;
remediation.apache:
# mod_headers – append the flags if missing
Header edit Set-Cookie ^(.*)$ "$1; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax"
remediation.cloudflare: Cloudflare cannot rewrite Set-Cookie; fix it at the origin or in the application framework.

findings.title: All cookies carry the HttpOnly flag
findings.description: HttpOnly stops JavaScript from reading the cookie, blunting session hijacking after an XSS.

findings.title: Server header discloses software version
findings.description: Version banners let attackers map the target to known CVEs; hide the token and patch promptly.

remediation.summary: Remove version banners from Server, X-Powered-By and X-AspNet-Version.  Banner grabbing is the first step of most targeted exploitation playbooks.
remediation.apache:
ServerTokens Prod
ServerSignature Off
<IfModule mod_headers.c>
    Header unset X-Powered-By
    Header unset X-AspNet-Version
    Header unset Server
</IfModule>
remediation.cloudflare: Cloudflare already strips/rewrites the Server header; add Transform Rules for X-Powered-By.

findings.title: security.txt is published and RFC 9116 compliant
findings.description: A valid security.txt is served with 1 contact(s) and a future Expires field.

findings.title: TLS certificate chain validates against the system trust store
findings.description: The leaf certificate chains to a trusted root and the hostname matches.

findings.title: TLS certificate expires in 22.5 days
findings.description: Certificates must be renewed before they expire; automate renewal and alert at 30 days.

remediation.summary: Renew the leaf certificate before it expires and monitor the remaining lifetime (alert at 30 days, page at 14).  Automate renewal with ACME.
remediation.nginx:
# certbot
certbot renew --quiet --deploy-hook "nginx -s reload"
# cron: 0 3 * * * certbot renew --quiet --deploy-hook "systemctl reload nginx"
remediation.cloudflare: Cloudflare managed certificates renew automatically – verify Edge Certificates shows an active cert.

findings.title: Deprecated TLSv1.0 is supported
findings.description: TLSv1.0 is deprecated by RFC 8996 and vulnerable to a long list of downgrade and padding-oracle attacks. Disable it and require TLS 1.2+.

remediation.summary: Disable TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 (deprecated by RFC 8996) and allow only TLS 1.2/1.3 with modern cipher suites.
remediation.cloudflare: SSL/TLS → Edge Certificates → Minimum TLS Version: TLS 1.2 (or TLS 1.3).

findings.title: Deprecated TLSv1.1 is disabled
findings.description: TLSv1.1 is deprecated by RFC 8996.

findings.title: TLS 1.3 is enabled
findings.description: TLS 1.3 removes legacy crypto and is faster.

findings.title: Negotiated cipher suite is strong
findings.description: The handshake selected an AEAD / forward-secret suite with adequate strength.

findings.title: Certificate covers example.com
findings.description: The hostname is present in the certificate's SAN extension.

findings.title: Plaintext HTTP redirects to HTTPS
findings.description: Port 80 answers with a redirect to the HTTPS origin.

findings.title: SPF record is published
findings.description: Exactly one v=spf1 record was found at the zone apex.

findings.title: SPF policy soft-fails (~all)
findings.description: SoftFail lets receivers accept the message but mark it as suspicious; move to -all once all legitimate senders are listed.

remediation.summary: Publish exactly one SPF record per domain, end it with -all (hard fail), keep the DNS-lookup count at or below 10 and remove deprecated mechanisms such as ptr.
remediation.dns:
example.com.        TXT  "v=spf1 mx include:_spf.example-provider.com -all"
# count lookups first:  https://www.kitterman.com/spf/validate.html
# >10 lookups? flatten includes or split transactional mail onto a subdomain:
mail.example.com.   TXT  "v=spf1 include:_spf.example-provider.com -all"

findings.title: SPF exceeds the 10-lookup limit (12)
findings.description: RFC 7208 caps a policy evaluation at 10 DNS lookups; exceeding it returns permerror and receivers ignore the record, re-enabling spoofing.

remediation.summary: Publish exactly one SPF record per domain, end it with -all (hard fail), keep the DNS-lookup count at or below 10 and remove deprecated mechanisms such as ptr.
remediation.dns:
example.com.        TXT  "v=spf1 mx include:_spf.example-provider.com -all"
# count lookups first:  https://www.kitterman.com/spf/validate.html
# >10 lookups? flatten includes or split transactional mail onto a subdomain:
mail.example.com.   TXT  "v=spf1 include:_spf.example-provider.com -all"

findings.title: DMARC record is published
findings.description: A DMARC policy is available to receivers.

findings.title: DMARC policy is monitor-only (p=none)
findings.description: p=none requests reports but tells receivers to deliver failing mail, so spoofing still reaches inboxes. Move to quarantine then reject.

remediation.summary: Publish a DMARC record with p=quarantine or p=reject and rua reporting so you can detect spoofing attempts and receive aggregate reports.
remediation.cloudflare: Cloudflare Email Security / DNS → add the TXT record at _dmarc.example.com. Keep Email Routing's own SPF/DKIM records intact.
remediation.dns:
_dmarc.example.com.  TXT  "v=DMARC1; p=reject; sp=reject; adkim=s; aspf=s; pct=100; fo=1; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@example.com; ruf=mailto:dmarc-forensics@example.com"
# rollout: start with p=none, review rua reports for 2-4 weeks, then move to p=quarantine and finally p=reject

findings.title: CAA records restrict certificate issuance
findings.description: Only the listed CAs may issue certificates for this domain.

findings.title: DNSSEC is not enabled
findings.description: Unsigned zones are vulnerable to cache-poisoning and forged DNS answers on the resolution path.

remediation.summary: Enable DNSSEC so resolvers can cryptographically validate your zone: publish DNSKEY/RRSIG in the zone and the matching DS record at the registrar/parent.
remediation.cloudflare: DNS → Settings → DNSSEC → Enable DNSSEC, then add the DS record at your registrar.
remediation.dns:
# after enabling DNSSEC at the provider, publish the DS record at the parent:
example.com.  IN DS  <keytag> <algorithm> <digest-type> <digest>
# verify:  dig +dnssec DNSKEY example.com  /  dig +trace DS example.com

findings.title: Dangling CNAME to a non-existent host (GitHub Pages)
findings.description: status.example.com is a CNAME to status-old.github.io, which does not resolve (NXDOMAIN). Whoever registers that endpoint inherits your hostname — remove or repoint the record.

remediation.summary: A CNAME points at a third-party endpoint that no longer exists — an attacker can often claim it and serve content on your domain.  Remove or repoint the record, or re-claim the service.
remediation.cloudflare: DNS → Records → delete or repoint the dangling CNAME, then purge the edge cache.
remediation.dns:
example.com.   IN CNAME   <active-provider-endpoint>
# or delete the record entirely:
# dig +short example.com CNAME  # confirm the chain is gone
